greeting: Hi, I'm Nova. This chat is in demo mode: I only have answers that were written in advance, and I'm not a live AI. Pick a question below, or type one and I'll try to match it to something I have.
fallback: I'm in demo mode, so I only have preset answers and I don't have one for that. I haven't looked it up or worked it out. Try one of the suggested questions, or mention a career by name (for example "Data Analyst").

prompts.question: Who are you, Nova?
prompts.answer: I'm Nova, the star-compass guide of PATHFINDER. Right now I'm a demo: my answers are written in advance and chosen by matching your words to a list. I'm not connected to a live AI model, so I can't reason about new questions.

prompts.question: What does a match score mean?
prompts.answer: Your quiz answers become a profile across eight dimensions, and every career has its own profile on the same eight. The match score is how closely the shape of the two lines up, using cosine similarity. 100% would mean an identical shape. It says nothing about how well you would do in the career.

prompts.question: Does a high score mean I would succeed?
prompts.answer: No. A match score compares your answers with a hand-written career profile. It does not measure ability, effort or how the job market treats you. Use it to decide what to read about and try, not to rule careers in or out.

prompts.question: What is Career DNA?
prompts.answer: It's your profile across the eight dimensions, drawn as a radar chart. It comes from your quiz answers, and you can edit it on the Career DNA page. Your matches update straight away. The sliders show how much each dimension stands out compared with your others, not how good you are at it.

prompts.question: I'm not sure where to start
prompts.answer: A good first step is the quiz: it asks about what you enjoy, what you can already do and how you like to work, and then shows careers with the reasons. You don't have to decide anything. Treat the results as a reading list. You can also browse Explore Careers or try Surprise Me.

prompts.question: Do I need to be good at maths?
prompts.answer: It varies by role. Data science and machine learning lean on statistics and linear algebra more. Many others, such as frontend, QA, design and product roles, lean on it less. That is a general picture, not a rule, and maths is learnable.

prompts.question: What do these careers pay?
prompts.answer: I don't have that data. Salary and demand show "data not connected yet" on every career page because I won't make up numbers. When they are connected, they will come with a source and an update date.

prompts.question: Do I need a law degree for cyber law?
prompts.answer: Practising as a lawyer in cyber law usually needs an LLB after your B.Tech. Some policy research and compliance roles do not require a law degree, but legal practice does.

prompts.question: Data Analyst or Data Scientist?
prompts.answer: They overlap. Analysts mostly answer business questions with SQL, spreadsheets and dashboards. Scientists lean more on statistics and modelling, including machine learning. Open both career pages to see their skills side by side. A comparison tool is planned but not built yet.

prompts.question: Where can I learn more?
prompts.answer: Career pages link to roadmap.sh roadmaps, only where a page has been checked to exist. I don't list courses because I won't invent links. Each page also has beginner project ideas you can start without a course.

prompts.question: Why is my top match my top match?
Can I change my answers?
prompts.answer: Yes. You can review and change quiz answers, adjust your Career DNA with the sliders, or retake the whole quiz. Retaking clears your answers and DNA edits but keeps your saved careers, and the results page shows how your matches moved.

prompts.question: Where is my data stored?
prompts.answer: Only in this browser, in local storage. There are no accounts and nothing is sent to a server. You can delete it all from the Privacy page.

prompts.question: What does Surprise Me do?
prompts.answer: On Explore Careers it suggests a career from an area you haven't looked at, picked because it shares dimensions with careers you matched or saved. With no profile yet, it picks something at random.
